newsitem.title: FRANCE: London Club agrees Ivory Coast debt plan - BNP.
newsitem.headline: London Club agrees Ivory Coast debt plan - BNP.

text.p: The London Club of commercial bank creditors has agreed the principles of a deal to restructure the Ivory Coast's $7.2 billion debt, French bank Banque Nationale de Paris announced on Friday.

"The principles of an agreement, which assumes the confirmation of support of financial backers, has been agreed to restructure the Ivory Coast debt which totals $7.2 billion," BNP said in a statement.
Some $4.6 billion of the commercial debt stems from interest accumulated since April 1987 when the west African nation ceased payments, BNP said.
The agreement followed a meeting which began on Wednesday and concluded on Friday attended by a delegation from the Ivory Coast led by Finance Minister N'Goran Niamien.

"The agreement, set to go into effect in mid-1997, will permit the Ivory Coast to restore the confidence of the international financial community and thus favour foreign investment in the country," the statement said.
The restructuring plan has been drafted along so-called Brady terms which take account of the Ivory Coast's specific economic conditions, BNP said.
The restructuring plan agreed with the steering committee of the country's creditor banks involves a buyback element, permitting the elimination of a minimum 30 percent of the debt.

For the remaining debt, two debt instruments will be issued at the discretion of the creditors -- a 30-year discount bond and a 20-year front-loaded interest-reduction par bond. There will also be a 20-year past-due interest bond.
The debt instruments will be issued in French francs and in dollars in proportions that respect the current breakdown of the debt in these two currencies.
